overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance data reveals that 'What If' space scenarios and extreme planetary physics are overwhelmingly outperforming standard fact formats. Videos employing speculative immersion ('What If You Fell Into...') combined with extreme visual hooks generate the highest views-per-day, likes-per-view, and active engagement ratios. Meanwhile, static psychological facts and older historical trivia are stagnating.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views) secured massive engagement soon after publishing compared to static fact videos.
winning_patterns.action: Prioritize 'What If' formatting over declarative statements, particularly focusing on bizarre planetary interactions.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' hit 1,026 views, showing high affinity for visually striking, counter-intuitive cosmic objects.
winning_patterns.action: Continue producing short-form content featuring extreme, rare cosmic anomalies with bold color contrast hooks.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' and psychological songs-stuck-in-your-head clips stalled out under 60 views.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standalone psychology facts unless framed as a high-stakes scenario or direct biological mystery.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'The 2,000-Year-Old Mystery Science Can't Solve' achieved minimal traction (139 views) with zero comments.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid vague historical mysteries; ensure any historical or archaeological topic features a tangible, shocking physical hazard or anomaly.
